name: Pounded bamboo soup
summary: A thick soup cooked in a bamboo tube and pounded with a chopstick so the greens, fish, and bitter eggplant bind. The Dak Lak provincial portal prints 60–90 minutes. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: The Dak Lak provincial portal, 18 Feb 2019, describes canh thụt as a highland soup and explains the name from the pounding.
howToEat: The portal lists lá bép, rattan shoots, bitter eggplant, stream fish or meat, fish sauce, chili, salt, MSG, and sugar. Cooks cut a lồ ô tube with a long joint and shape the mouth so the soup cannot leak. A tube that is too old splits. A tube that is too young tastes wrong. Everything goes in, the tube leans on the fire, and someone turns it and pounds the contents with a chopstick so they mix and steam escapes.

The portal says a tube is usually under half a metre, and that a festival may need many tubes. It prints 60–90 minutes to cook. Finished soup is thick and sticky, served in a bowl or on a banana leaf. The tastes it names are bitter, hot, nutty, and fatty. A price is Check on arrival. A street was not printed.
where: The portal does not name a street in Buon Ma Thuot. Where to order it is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Canh thut in Dak Lak — soup pounded in a bamboo tube
seoDescription: Thick soup of forest greens, bitter eggplant, and stream fish or meat, cooked and pounded in a bamboo tube for 60–90 minutes. A street and a price are Check on arrival.
taste: The Dak Lak provincial portal says the finished soup is thick and sticky, and tastes bitter, hot, nutty, and fatty.
